Yep, investment is the word.

If you buy stock in a company and the company goes belly up, you don't complain to the stock exchange for a refund. Investment carries the risk of loss. It always has, and it always will.

Whether or not there are the means have "handling mismanagement" doesn't determine whether or not it's an investment. Whether or not there is an expectation of return would be closer to determining that, and people back Kickstarter campaigns with a very explicit expectation of return.

A Kickstarter campaign is the alternative to going to a Venture Capitalist. There are risks involved and not every investment guarantees a return. The difference between KC and VCs is that a VC expects a 1000% return on investment - that is the price of high risk.

But before an investment is made by a VC or a KC backer, due diligence is required. Not just dotting all the i's and crossing all the t's, but putting together steps towards accountability. Fraud is Fraud, that's why it is essential to protect yourself and your company, brand and reputation.

I hate to see investors lose their investment, but I'm hopeful that after we see enough of these kinds of stories, we can shift the momentum away from this oblivious approach to throwing money at games that sound good to the thoughtful approach of investing money in games being made by teams that are showing potential. When someone launches a Kickstarter campaign to fund early development costs of a game and they set their goal to $20k, that sends a very loud message to me. It tells me that this person is most likely underestimating the cost involved in development by an enormous margin, and if they don't have the project management savvy to come up with a more realistic figure the chances of them having the chops to see the project to fruition are not good.

Every experienced investor evaluates part of the risk based on whether or not they think the potential recipient is asking a reasonable amount for what they claim to want to do. Asking too little shows a lack of confidence and unrealistic expectations.

We need to correct this culture of doing stupid things over and over again and then crying to someone else to save us. At some point, we need to start learning from our mistakes.
